sources.title: Slocombe et al. (2023). Overexpression of PSR1 in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii induces luxury phosphorus uptake
sources.limit: Reported batch cultures; regulatory explanation includes an author-proposed mechanism. Existing quantitative demo records remain separate.

sources.title: Guan et al. (2023). The cytoplasmic synthesis and coupled membrane translocation of eukaryotic polyphosphate by signal-activated VTC complex
sources.locator: Abstract; Introduction Vtc1/Vtc2/Vtc4 and Vtc1/Vtc3/Vtc4 complexes
sources.limit: Targeted abstract/introduction review. Exact strains and construct-to-reference accessions have not been admitted.

sources.title: García Martín et al. (2006). Metagenomic analysis of two enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR) sludge communities
sources.limit: Community metagenomic evidence; individual gene necessity, exact loci and purified-isolate sufficiency are not established by this admitted abstract.

sources.title: Jensen et al. (1996). Enhanced effectiveness of copper ion buffering by CUP1 metallothionein compared with CRS5 metallothionein in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
sources.limit: Copper buffering and resistance; not environmental removal, broad metal specificity or safe disposal. Exact strain/accession mapping remains open.

sources.title: The CUP2 gene product, regulator of yeast metallothionein expression, is a copper-activated DNA-binding protein (1989)
sources.limit: Native regulatory evidence does not establish recipient regulatory compatibility.

sources.title: Mach et al. (1999). Expression of two major chitinase genes of Trichoderma atroviride (T. harzianum P1) is triggered by different regulatory signals
sources.locator: Abstract, ech42/nag1 expression on fungal cell walls and chitin products
sources.limit: Expression/regulation study. This is fungal cell-wall substrate evidence, not proof of whole-biomass conversion or contaminated-algae processing.

sources.title: Donzelli and Harman (2001). Interaction of ammonium, glucose, and chitin regulates the expression of cell wall-degrading enzymes in Trichoderma atroviride strain P1
sources.locator: Abstract, interacting carbon/nitrogen effects on expression and secretion
sources.limit: Context-dependent enzyme expression/secretion; does not qualify a receiving organism or a mixed biomass stream.

sources.title: Chalfie et al. (1994). Green fluorescent protein as a marker for gene expression
sources.locator: Abstract, Aequorea victoria cDNA expressed in E. coli and C. elegans
sources.limit: Documented heterologous reporting in these study contexts; not universal transfer or proof that fluorescence measures another desired trait.

sources.title: Heim, Prasher and Tsien (1994). Wavelength mutations and posttranslational autoxidation of green fluorescent protein
sources.limit: Maturation conditions are construct/context dependent. No reporter calibration in a proposed recipient has been admitted.

sources.title: Bajhaiya et al. (2016). PSR1 Is a Global Transcriptional Regulator of Phosphorus Deficiency Responses and Carbon Storage Metabolism in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
sources.locator: Abstract, starch increase and neutral-lipid decrease
sources.limit: Different endpoints and source backgrounds; not a direct contradiction of the phosphorus uptake study.

sources.title: Gerasimaitė et al. (2014). Coupled synthesis and translocation restrains polyphosphate to acidocalcisome-like vacuoles and prevents its toxicity
sources.locator: Abstract, cytosolic toxicity and coupled vacuolar import
sources.limit: A compartment-specific safety constraint, not a universal toxicity estimate.

sources.title: Woo et al. (1999). Disruption of the ech42 (Endochitinase-Encoding) Gene Affects Biocontrol Activity in Trichoderma harzianum P1
sources.limit: Biocontrol endpoints differ by host; neither expression nor one perturbation is whole-biomass conversion evidence.

sources.title: Drepper et al. (2010). Flavin Mononucleotide-Based Fluorescent Reporter Proteins Outperform Green Fluorescent Protein-Like Proteins as Quantitative In Vivo Real-Time Reporters
sources.locator: Abstract, oxygen-limited E. coli batch cultures
sources.limit: Reporter-family/context comparison; does not negate the existence of GFP fluorescence.

traits.name: Regulated phosphate uptake
traits.context: PSR1-overexpressing lines in the UVM4 background; laboratory batch cultures with phosphate initially available
traits.endpoint: Phosphate uptake and cellular phosphorus; recovered-product yield is separate

claims.text: PSR1-overexpressing lines showed enhanced phosphate uptake and cellular phosphorus relative to UVM4 in the reported cultures.
A regulator acts through native transport, storage and nutrient-response machinery; a PSR1-only transfer cannot be assumed to recreate that network.
claims.locator: Discussion feed-forward model; transfer boundary is curator inference

claims.text: Investigate whether a receiving context has compatible regulation and phosphorus handling before considering trait transfer.

traits.name: Intracellular copper binding
traits.context: Native metallothionein and regulatory studies; specific copper exposure comparisons; exact strain/reference unresolved
traits.endpoint: Cu(I) buffering and copper resistance; not recovered-metal yield

claims.text: CUP1 and CRS5 comparisons supported a strong role for Cup1 in copper buffering and resistance; promoter context affected the outcome.
CUP2 was characterized as a copper-responsive transcriptional activator of CUP1.
Binding capacity, regulation and intracellular copper access must be considered separately from environmental capture.
Investigate recipient copper handling and expression context before evaluating a metal-binding application.

dependencies.requirement: Copper speciation, intracellular access and toxicity
dependencies.check: Separate binding, survival and net metal removal in the intended context.
Resolve stock-specific regulation without assuming native promoters function across species.

open_questions: What metal species and compartment are relevant?
Where does retained copper go after biomass collection?
traits.safety: Copper remains hazardous after binding. Human review must address exposure, residuals and disposal; binding does not detoxify the environment by itself.

dossier.evidence_map: organism/context → observed trait → supported gene/protein associations → dependencies → recipient gaps

conflicts_and_caveats.text: The promoter-exchange comparison changed metallothionein-associated resistance. Protein identity alone does not determine the native outcome. No conflicting environmental-removal trial is admitted.

missing_information: Metal speciation, exact stock and gene-copy/reference identity
Residual exposure, disposal and recovery endpoints

traits.name: Fungal cell-wall breakdown system
traits.context: Strain P1 (historically T. harzianum P1), fungal cell walls and chitin-related substrates; enzyme expression/secretion studies
traits.endpoint: Chitinolytic enzyme expression and secretion; whole-biomass conversion not quantified here

claims.text: ech42 and nag1 showed different regulatory responses to fungal cell walls and chitin degradation products.
Carbon and nitrogen context affected cell-wall-degrading enzyme expression and secretion in strain P1.

traits.name: Green fluorescent reporting
traits.context: Native jellyfish GFP; separate published heterologous reporting in E. coli and C. elegans
traits.endpoint: Fluorescent signal; interpretation requires context-specific controls

claims.text: Aequorea victoria GFP cDNA produced fluorescent protein in E. coli and C. elegans in the reported study.
Formation of the mature GFP fluorophore required molecular oxygen in the reported characterization.
Fluorescence is a reporter readout; it does not by itself establish phosphorus uptake, protein activity or another phenotype.
Investigate expression, maturation and background fluorescence in the exact recipient before assigning a reporting role.
